equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2027 guidance update 21-Aug-2026: NZ$23m refund following the US Supreme Court IEEPA ruling; kept out of the recurring EBITDA-margin path and added here once, undiscounted (immaterial at NZ$0.04/share).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Trailing 3yr/5yr windows diverge by >30% from each other and from the through-cycle rate because every window starting or ending in FY2021-FY2023 is distorted by the COVID hardware pull-forward (FY2021 revenue 1,971 vs 1,264 in FY2020) and the FY2023 trough (owner FCF 15.1 on capex peak + inventory build). 5yr EPS CAGR is negative and 5yr equity CAGR 6.8% for the same reason. Selected rate is the FY2019->FY2026 through-cycle revenue CAGR (11.6%), which brackets one full pre-COVID to post-COVID cycle; EPS (11.8%) and equity (12.8%) through-cycle CAGRs cluster within 1.2pp of it.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs use the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less interest income): FY2019 111.0 -> FY2026 445.9 (CSV FCF basis, lease repayments not deducted in the history because IFRS 16 only applies from FY2020). Owner-FCF through-cycle CAGR 22.0% vs reported 21.5%: SBC (0.5% -> 0.6% of revenue) is not outgrowing cash flow. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR (FY2023 base of 15.1) is meaningless and left null. FY2024 reported NPAT (132.6, 7.6% margin) is a one-off low (product-recall provision, NZ$98.1m land revaluation, NZ building-depreciation tax change); underlying NPAT was 264.4.

scenario_narratives.base: FPH compounds revenue at ~9-10% for the next four years on the two axes that have driven it for a decade: 'changing clinical practice' pulling nasal high flow (Optiflow/Airvo 3, F&P 950) into emergency, COPD, post-operative and anesthesia use, and a steady OSA mask cadence (Nova Nasal, Nova Micro, Vitera, Evora, Solo) holding a top-3 share against ResMed and Philips. Consumables (~90% of both segments) keep growth largely independent of hospital admission seasons. Gross margin climbs toward the 65% constant-currency target from 63.7%, taking EBITDA from 34.4% to 36.5%. Capex runs hot at 9.5-9.8% of revenue through FY2028 for the fifth East Tamaki building and Karaka, then normalises. Growth consumes working capital at 10% of the revenue increase. Terminal value is the lower of Gordon at 3.5%/9.0% and 20x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The December-2024 JAMA trial and GOLD guidance make nasal high flow the default therapy for hypoxemic respiratory failure across US and European EDs, hospital hardware placements (Airvo 3, 950) seed a step-up in consumables, Nova Micro takes OSA share, and the Guangzhou site opens China at scale. Gross margin reaches 65% by FY2030 and opex leverage lifts EBITDA to 39.5%; capex intensity falls below 6% once the campus programme completes; growth stays double-digit for four years. The 4.0% terminal growth reflects the NZ$25bn+ addressable market against ~NZ$2.3bn of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: Revenue growth halves to mid-single digits: US hospital admission normalisation and a slower ED/COPD adoption curve blunt Hospital consumables, ResMed's AirSense/mask cadence and a recovered Philips cap Homecare share, and reported margins are compressed by a stronger NZD and new US tariffs on NZ- and Mexico-made product that the IEEPA refund does not protect against. EBITDA settles at ~33%, capex overruns at East Tamaki/Karaka absorb cash through FY2029, and the market's willingness to pay a scarcity premium fades; terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A component-built owner-FCF DCF at a currency-matched 9.0% NZD WACC values FPH at roughly half the ASX price, in line with the companion FPH.NZ valuation. This is the honest output of capitalising the cash flows at a market-consistent discount rate, not a modelling defect: FPH has traded at 30-60x trailing earnings and ~30x EV/EBITDA for most of its listed history because the market accepts a forward IRR well below 9% to own a scarce, net-cash, razor/razorblade global compounder. The sensitivity grid and bull case show what has to be true to reach the price (EBITDA margins near 40%, double-digit growth for four years and a terminal growth rate above 4%, or a WACC around 7%). Treat the DCF as the conservative anchor and the ASX price as embedding a persistent scarcity/quality premium; for an ASX holder the AUD/NZD cross adds a translation layer on top of the underlying NZD result.
key_risks_to_valuation: FX: ~99% of revenue is non-NZD (USD ~50%, EUR ~20%) against a NZD/MXN cost base; a 5% stronger NZD is worth roughly 2pp of reported EBITDA margin once hedges roll off, and the AUD quote adds NZD/AUD translation for ASX holders
US tariff policy on NZ- and Mexico-sourced hospital product: the FY2027 IEEPA refund is one-off and the modelled margins assume current tariff rates persist
Capex supercycle: fifth East Tamaki building and Karaka campus keep capex at 9.5-11% of revenue through FY2028; overruns or delayed revenue from the new capacity compress FCF conversion
Terminal value is ~60-65% of enterprise value; each 50bp of terminal growth or WACC moves the base IV by roughly 8-10%
Competitive cadence in OSA masks (ResMed, Philips) and hospital respiratory (Vyaire, Getinge, Draeger); a product recall (FY2024 precedent) or IP litigation would hit both margins and multiple
Multiple compression independent of operations: the market price sits far above every scenario, so a de-rating toward the DCF band needs no operating disappointment to occur

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: FY2026 annual report note 16 diluted weighted-average shares 590,996,952 (587,276,425 issued at 31 Mar 2026 plus ~3.7m dilutive employee share-plan shares/options). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the FPH.NZ file compounds the count 0.0556%/yr on top of expensing SBC, a minor double-charge not repeated here. No non-SBC issuance; DRP suspended.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Company definition (FY2026 AR p.126): operating cash flow 663.2 less capex 195.2 less lease liability repayments 21.4 = 446.6. The Metrics CSV FreeCashFlow (468.0) is OCF less capex without the lease repayment; the company figure is used here because lease treatment (B) charges the lease inside the flows.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: Stripped. Net cash NZ$401.3m is 0.9x the owner-FCF base; interest income (P&L 8.2, cash received 7.3) is removed so the cash pile is not counted once in the flows and again in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report cash flow reconciliation, 'Share based payments' 13.9 (FY2025: 11.2). No net-share-settlement tax withholding disclosed (shares issued under employee plans, 4.2 proceeds in financing), so equity-award taxes = 0.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in any year of the history; the flat count is a modelling convention funded by expensing SBC, not by a buyback programme.
inputs.fx_note: NZD->AUD 0.8055, Yahoo Finance NZDAUD=X at 2026-09-22T11:29Z (52-week 0.8003-0.8896). Parity check against the primary NZX listing: FPH.NZ NZ$44.98 (2026-09-22T04:59Z close) x 0.8055 = A$36.23 vs observed FPH.AX A$36.20, a 0.1% tie confirming rate, direction and quote basis. All flows and per-share values are built in NZD and converted to AUD at this rate; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are in AUD (quote currency), NZD twins are suffixed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in NZD, the currency of the flows: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.4% + 5.5% equity risk premium x ~0.85 beta for a net-cash global medical-device compounder, ~9.0-9.4% cost of equity; with net cash and immaterial borrowings WACC = cost of equity. 9.0% is used for ALL THREE scenarios (owner-fcf-adaptations (f): risk charged once, in the flows). FX-translation and US-tariff risk are modelled in the bear driver paths, not as a bear-scenario WACC premium; the companion FPH.NZ file uses 8.0/9.0/10.5 per scenario, which stacks the risk twice.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. FY2026 lease liability principal 21.4 (financing) + lease interest paid 4.5 (operating) = 25.9 = 1.12% of revenue, charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (86.3) EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (132.2, 5.7% of revenue; total D&A incl. ROU 158.6). The FPH.NZ file charges neither (no lease line, lease liabilities out of net debt) and uses full D&A; the difference is ~NZ$0.35/share.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: no minority interests; all profit attributable to shareholders of the parent.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2, operating company, non-US filer with a quote currency different from the reporting currency -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md sections (a1), (a2), (b), (f)). FPH is a profitable razor/razorblade medical-device manufacturer (Hospital 63% / Homecare 37%, ~90% consumables) reporting in NZD; FPH.AX is the ASX secondary quotation of the same ordinary shares quoted in AUD. FRESH BUILD for this ticker (no prior FPH.AX Drivers/DCF); the driver judgments are carried from the FPH.NZ valuation of 2026-08-11 (same business) with these deliberate changes, each stated: (1) year-1 growth and margin refreshed to the 21-Aug-2026 guidance raise; (2) leases charged once under treatment (B); (3) working-capital capture NEGATIVE (manufacturer: receivables + inventories exceed payables, net working capital 19% of revenue); (4) one WACC for all scenarios; (5) share count flat. Later-year growth, EBITDA-margin maturity (36.5%), capex glide, cash-tax path, terminal growth and cap multiple are UNCHANGED from FPH.NZ. bear.rationale: FY2027 misses the guidance floor on a weak H2 (+6.5%); a stronger NZD against USD/EUR (99% of revenue non-NZD, hedge cover thinning beyond FY2028-29) and renewed US tariffs on NZ/Mexico-sourced product hold EBITDA margins at 32.5-33.4%; construction overruns at East Tamaki/Karaka keep capex at 10.5-11% for three years. WACC held at 9.0% (not FPH.NZ's 10.5%): FX and tariff risk are charged here in the flows and the 15x cap, not again in the discount rate.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 = midpoint of the raised FY2027 revenue guidance NZ$2.47-2.57bn (2.52bn, +9.2%; H1 guided ~1.24bn, +14%, so the full-year midpoint assumes a softer H2 comp). Years 2-3 at 10.5% follow the FY2019-26 through-cycle 11.6% less a point for the larger base; decelerating to 4.0% by year 10 as nasal-high-flow practice change matures. Unchanged from FPH.NZ beyond year 1.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 EBITDA margin 34.4% (795.0/2308.4). FY2027 guidance NPAT 525-565 on 2.52bn implies ~36.0% EBITDA incl. the NZ$23m refund, ~35.1% excluding it; year 1 set at 35.0% ex-refund. Path rises 150bps over 10 years on the 65% constant-currency gross-margin target (FY2026 63.7%) with modest opex leverage; 36.5% maturity unchanged from FPH.NZ.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 capex 195.2 = 8.5% of revenue including the second Karaka land parcel. Fifth East Tamaki building (~NZ$250m, operational 2027) and Karaka campus keep capex at 9.5-9.8% through FY2028, then glide to 6.5% (pre-supercycle run-rate ~7-9% of a smaller base). D&A ex-ROU (5.7% in FY2026) rises to 7.3% as the new building depreciates then settles at 6.3%, 20bps under terminal capex for a still-growing asset base.
base.wc_rationale: Net working capital (receivables 329.4 + inventories 327.3 - payables 300.1 = 356.6, 15% of revenue; company definition 447.2, 19%) means growth consumes cash. FY2025/26 releases (+16.0, -6.9) came from post-COVID destocking that is now complete (inventories -15.6 in FY2026 while revenue grew 14%). -10% capture of the revenue increase: below the 15-19% structural intensity to credit ongoing inventory efficiency.
base.tax_rationale: FY2026 cash tax 161.4 on PBT ~631 = 25.6%; effective rate 25.8% (29.2% excluding the NZ R&D tax credit). Path ramps to 27% as the R&D credit shrinks relative to profit; NZ statutory 28%.

bull.rationale: Year 1 at the top of guidance (2.57bn, +11.3%). Nasal high flow becomes standard of care in ED/COPD/anesthesia, Nova/Nova Micro win OSA mask share from ResMed and Philips, the 65% gross-margin target is reached by FY2030 with opex leverage taking EBITDA to 39.5%. WACC held at 9.0% (not FPH.NZ's 8.0%): the upside is in the flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (house default 15%, +5pp): no solvency or covenant risk, but two exogenous swing factors (NZD strength against a 99% non-NZD revenue base with hedge cover thinning beyond FY2028-29, and US tariff policy on NZ/Mexico-sourced product) can each cut reported margins independently of execution. Bull 30% (house default 35%, -5pp): the bull case needs three things at once (65% gross margin reached, double-digit growth sustained on a NZ$2.3bn base, capex intensity below 6%), though the August-2026 guidance raise shows momentum. Base 50%. FPH.NZ used 25/50/25.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
